Below is a quick‑start guide you can follow for **any** new tabular dataset, plus a ready‑to‑use prompt template you can paste into a LLM (or a data‑science notebook) once you fill in the missing details. --- ## 1️⃣ Typical workflow for a new dataset | Phase | Goal | Typical actions | Why it matters | |-------|------|----------------|----------------| | **1️⃣ Data inventory** | Know what you have | • List all files/tables
• Record column names, types, and brief description of each field | Prevents surprises later (e.g., hidden timestamps, encoded categories) | | **2️⃣ Data quality check** | Spot problems early | • Count missing values per column
• Detect duplicates, out‑of‑range values, inconsistent formats (dates, currencies)
• Verify unique identifiers | Bad data → biased models & wasted time | | **3️⃣ Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)** | Understand distributions & relationships | • Histograms / box‑plots for numeric columns
• Bar charts for categoricals
• Correlation matrix / pair‑plots
• Simple cross‑tabulations (e.g., target vs. category) | Guides feature engineering & model choice | | **4️⃣ Pre‑processing / Feature engineering** | Turn raw data into model‑ready inputs | • Impute or drop missing values (mean/median, KNN, model‑based)
• Encode categoricals (one‑hot, target encoding, embeddings)
• Scale/normalize numeric features (StandardScaler, MinMax)
• Create new features (date parts, ratios, text embeddings) | Improves model performance & stability | | **5️⃣ Train‑test split & validation strategy** | Estimate real‑world performance | • Random split (e.g., 80/20) or time‑based split if data is temporal
• Consider cross‑validation (k‑fold, stratified) | Prevents over‑fitting and gives reliable metrics | | **6️⃣ Model selection & baseline** | Find a good starting point | • Simple baseline (e.g., mean predictor, logistic regression)
• Try a few algorithms (tree‑based, linear, neural nets) with default hyper‑parameters | Baseline tells you whether the problem is easy or hard | | **7️⃣ Hyper‑parameter tuning** | Squeeze extra performance | • Grid search, random search, or Bayesian optimization
• Use validation set or cross‑validation scores | Small tweaks can give big gains | | **8️⃣ Evaluation & diagnostics** | Verify that the model works | • Choose appropriate metrics (RMSE, MAE, ROC‑AUC, F1, etc.)
• Plot residuals, calibration curves, confusion matrix
• Check for data leakage or over‑fitting | Guarantees you’re not chasing a phantom improvement | | **9️⃣ Deployment / reporting** | Turn the work into value | • Export model (pickle, ONNX, TorchScript, etc.)
• Write a concise report: data description, methodology, results, next steps
• Set up monitoring if the model will run in production | Makes the project usable by stakeholders | --- ## 2️⃣ Prompt template to extract the *best* insights from the dataset > **Prompt (fill in the placeholders in **bold**):** > > ``` > You are a data‑science assistant. I have a dataset stored in **[file_path_or_table_name]** with the following schema: > > | Column | Data type | Brief description | > |--------|-----------|-------------------| > | **col1** | **type1** | **desc1** | > | **col2** | **type2** | **desc2** | > | … | > > The target variable (if any) is **[target_column]** and the problem type is **[classification / regression / clustering / anomaly detection]**. > > Please perform the full end‑to‑end analysis: > 1. Summarize data quality (missingness, duplicates, obvious outliers). > 2. Provide an exploratory data analysis summary (key distributions, top correlations, any surprising patterns). > 3. Suggest a minimal preprocessing pipeline (imputation, encoding, scaling) and justify each step. > 4. Build a quick baseline model (choose a simple algorithm appropriate for the problem) and report its performance using **[metric1, metric2]**. > 5. Recommend two more advanced models to try, with a short rationale for eac
